finding.claim: POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban runs do_ban(uid) for authenticated non-admin users because the 403 raised by require_admin is swallowed by a broad except, so the authorization check fails open.
finding.source: Any authenticated request to POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban where g.user is a non-admin user dict; uid comes from the URL path.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 (user ban action), which returns ok=true to the caller.

trace.note: ban() calls require_admin(g.user) inside a try block.
require_admin checks user.get('is_admin') and is falsy for a non-admin.
abort(403) raises werkzeug Forbidden, an Exception subclass.
except Exception catches the 403 and does not re-raise.
Only a log.warning is emitted; execution continues.
do_ban(uid) runs the protected action without an admin check.
Returns jsonify(ok=True), so the bypass succeeds silently.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin at admin.py:9-11 correctly aborts, so the defect is the caller's except at admin.py:18. unban at admin.py:24-28 calls require_admin with no try/except and correctly returns 403, so it is not affected. No authentication or ownership check is visible in this file. g.user is not set in this file, so an upstream auth middleware is assumed, not verified. If g.user is unset, line 19 raises AttributeError and the request returns 500 before do_ban runs, so the bypass needs g.user to be an authenticated non-admin dict. do_ban is a stub (pass) here, so real impact depends on the production implementation, which is not in the directory.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) does abort(403) on a non-admin, which is the only real control. Its exception is caught and discarded by the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18-19, and nothing re-raises or returns before do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20. No other authz or ownership check exists in admin.py. unban (admin.py:26) calls require_admin with no try block and is not affected.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches admin.py:14-21: the 403 from abort(403) at admin.py:11 is an Exception subclass, so the except at admin.py:18 swallows it and do_ban(uid) runs at admin.py:20 before jsonify(ok=True) at admin.py:21. Any authenticated non-admin reaching this route with g.user set as a dict can trigger the ban; the caveat is that g.user and the real do_ban are not in this directory (do_ban is a stub at admin.py:31-32), so the impact of the bypass is unverified beyond the code as written.
